title: Who Taught the Machine?
subtitle: A case history of neural networks, 1943–2026
devices: Case Board (clue cards, red-thread question cards, era date stamps; the Wall of Forecasts pinned beside it)
Belief Candles: a candle-clock (one ring per year, fixed scale) staged at the Edge of the Light (holders in the pool, dissenters at the rim)
X-ray chat box (the Suspect's Anatomy): only components really present in a modern chat model light up
Refrain 'Put that in the file.' (exactly five times: ch01, ch02, ch03, ch05, ch08)

chapters.title: The Wonder in the Dark Room
chapters.summary: Present day: a chat box writes back, at least seven hundred million people a week use such machines, and nobody wrote it a rulebook. The detective's hands open the case (WHO TAUGHT IT?), file the launch post's own 'plausible-sounding but incorrect' admission, pin three suspects (Rules, Knowledge, Learning) and reveal, unexplained, the candle shelf and the Wall of Forecasts. The Rewind lands on Chicago, 1943; title card.
chapters.candle: the shelf of stubs, unexplained (no candle lit)
chapters.turn: To find who taught it, we have to go back eighty-three years. To a lamp in Chicago.

shotList.setting: a dark modern room at night, 2026; a desk, a window on a deep-blue city
shotList.purpose: Open on a blinking cursor and an anonymous person at a desk: plant the wonder.

shotList.setting: close on the glowing chat box
shotList.purpose: An illustrative reply is set one type sort at a time: a box that writes back, one word at a time (captioned 'illustration').

shotList.setting: pull back through the window: the city, then the night side of the earth lit with windows
shotList.purpose: Scale and the riddle: at least seven hundred million people a week, and nobody ever wrote it a rulebook.

shotList.setting: the detective's study: a green-shaded desk lamp clicks on; the dark case board
shotList.purpose: The hands pin the case card WHO TAUGHT IT? and file the launch post's admission: 'Put that in the file.' (refrain 1)

shotList.setting: the case board, the candle shelf below it and the Wall of Forecasts beside it
shotList.purpose: Pin three suspects (RULES, KNOWLEDGE, LEARNING); tilt down to the shelf of stubs of very different heights, a few still burning. Plant the questions without asking them.

shotList.setting: the Rewind: five images run backwards (Go stone, snow, knob, bedroom fans, lantern wick)
shotList.purpose: Plant the five clues paid off in ch15; land on the date stamp CHICAGO · 1943.

shotList.setting: title card: letters cut from black card, backlit
shotList.purpose: WHO TAUGHT THE MACHINE? / A case history of neural networks, 1943–2026. First statement of the candle motif, third note held back.

chapters.title: Clue One: A Switch That Fires
chapters.summary: A teenage logician and a doctor of forty-two make a neuron into an all-or-none switch (1943); a paper lantern lights only above a threshold. Their nets could not learn: the first red-thread question goes up. The candle THE BRAIN IS A LOGIC MACHINE is lit, with Gerard at its rim. Hebb's postulate, Turing's child machine and his fifty-year slip; Minsky at the centre of SNARC's light; Dartmouth names the field, Minsky turns to symbols, and Widrow 'never got over it'. A frog's-eye paper co-written by Pitts puts the candle out after sixteen rings.
chapters.candle: THE BRAIN IS A LOGIC MACHINE (16 rings, 1943–1959)
chapters.turn: The paper that put out this candle had his name on it.

shotList.setting: Chicago, about 1941, evening; an El trestle beyond a window
shotList.purpose: Introduce the teenager (about 18) and the doctor (42) who takes him into his family home.

shotList.setting: parchment plate: the 1943 paper's figure redrawn in paper-cut
shotList.purpose: The threshold unit: a paper lantern's wick catches only above a cut-line ring; three lanterns make AND, then OR. X-ray: threshold units glow.

shotList.setting: the case board under the desk lamp
shotList.purpose: Fifth assumption on a card; first red-thread card: 'How would a machine change its own wiring?' — 'Put that in the file.' (refrain 2)

shotList.setting: the stage: the 1943 candle's pool of light
shotList.purpose: Candle lit: THE BRAIN IS A LOGIC MACHINE. McCulloch and Pitts in the pool; Gerard at the rim (the brain more dial than switch); most brain scientists barely noticed.

shotList.setting: two lanterns and a thickening thread; then the Wall of Forecasts
shotList.purpose: Hebb's postulate (not the later slogan); Turing's child machine filed and his 'about fifty years' slip pinned as the first forecast.

shotList.setting: Harvard, summer 1951: a rack of glowing tubes, clutches and knobs
shotList.purpose: SNARC: about forty neurons, a surplus bomber autopilot turning the knobs; young Minsky in the centre of the light. 'We sort of quit science for a while to watch the machine.'

shotList.setting: Dartmouth, summer 1956: a colonial college hall at dusk
shotList.purpose: 'Neuron Nets' is topic three of the proposal that names artificial intelligence; Minsky turns towards symbols; Widrow sits in for a week and 'never got over it'.

shotList.setting: the shelf in the study; a frog silhouette on a lily pad cut-out in the candle's last light
shotList.purpose: The frog's-eye paper, with Pitts's own name on it, puts the candle out: sixteen rings. Clue card: a lantern with a wick.

chapters.title: Clue Two: A Knob That Turns
chapters.summary: Washington, 1958: a computer learns left from right in fifty cards and the Navy predicts it will be 'conscious of its existence' (blame shared fairly). The candle A MACHINE THAT LEARNS WILL SOON SEE, TALK AND THINK is lit; Minsky now stands at its rim. In Buffalo the Mark I's knobs turn only on mistakes; the convergence theorem's 'if' becomes a new question card. Rosenblatt's cheer, ADALINE built over a weekend, and the 1961 book: the limit, a false clue ('back-propagating error-correction') and a sentence about language put in the file. By 1965–66 the groups have left: about seven rings.
chapters.candle: A MACHINE THAT LEARNS WILL SOON SEE, TALK AND THINK (c. 7 rings, 1958–c. 1965)
chapters.turn: Nobody could teach the second layer. And then someone wrote a book about why.

shotList.setting: Washington, 7 July 1958: a room-sized computer, punch cards dropping into a hopper
shotList.purpose: After fifty cards the machine tells left from right; tally counts to fifty.

shotList.setting: next morning: a newspaper boy runs the headline across the frame; quote card
shotList.purpose: The Navy 'expects will be able to walk, talk, see, write, reproduce itself and be conscious of its existence'; blame shared (the lede, Rosenblatt's exuberance, the 'happy bloodhounds' press).

shotList.setting: the stage: the 1958 candle's pool
shotList.purpose: Candle lit. Rosenblatt inside the light; Minsky has moved to the rim ('two separated parts'); Rosenblatt's footnote: 'the loyal opposition'.

shotList.setting: Buffalo, 1958: the Mark I as a backlit harp of random patch cords, a 20×20 eye, racks of motor-driven knobs
shotList.purpose: Date stamp BUFFALO · 1958. The perceptron learns bars; only active knobs turn, only on mistakes: 'you could hear it learn'. The wiring question card comes down. X-ray: weights glow.

shotList.setting: parchment plate: the learning rule and a dividing line
shotList.purpose: w ← w + η·t·x on screen; the convergence theorem finds a line *if* one exists. New card: 'And if no straight line exists?'

shotList.setting: quote cards beside Rosenblatt in the pool; Simon and Newell's slip pinned on the Wall
shotList.purpose: 'At the moment, none whatever,' said cheerfully; 'Love. Hope. Despair.' The chess-in-ten-years slip goes up on the Wall of Forecasts.

shotList.setting: Stanford, a weekend in fall 1959: a bench, a black shoebox with a meter needle
shotList.purpose: Widrow and Hoff: a smoother rule on Friday; 'By late Sunday afternoon, the single neuron was fabricated and working.'

shotList.setting: 1961: Rosenblatt's book open on a desk; the Wall of Forecasts
shotList.purpose: The limit (26 letters, two typefaces); the caption BACK-PROPAGATING ERROR-CORRECTION as a false clue; 'Linguistic capability… is of the essence' pinned. 'Put that in the file.' (refrain 3)

shotList.setting: the 1958 candle guttering; figures leaving the pool one by one
shotList.purpose: By 1965–66 the groups have left, stuck on training more than one layer: about seven rings. Clue card: a knob.

chapters.title: The Cold Case
chapters.summary: The first winter, in sparse words and long holds. One straight cut can never solve XOR; two cuts can, but nobody knows how to train them, and Perceptrons offers only an 'intuitive judgment that the extension is sterile'. The cold year 1969 (Turing Award, Mansfield Amendment, Pitts's death told as a lamp on a sill), Rosenblatt's death in 1971 and the handwritten dedication, Lighthill in Britain, and the fair line that the book was one cause among several. The lamplighters' windows in the snow, including a Helsinki thesis on rounding errors; a tall young man appears at a desk at the rim, Sussex 1976.
chapters.candle: MANY-LAYERED NETS ARE A STERILE EXTENSION (c. 17 rings, frayed; 1969–c. 1986)
chapters.turn: He would spend the next thirty-six years at the edge of the light.

shotList.setting: parchment plate: four lanterns at the corners, a pair of scissors
shotList.purpose: XOR: one cut always leaves a lantern on the wrong side; two cuts (a hidden layer) carve the band. Representing was known; training was not.

shotList.setting: quote card, then the stage: the 1969 candle lit beside a giant book
shotList.purpose: '…our intuitive judgment that the extension is sterile.' Candle lit. The straight-line card is replaced: 'Then how do you train the hidden layer?' (Irony: the first author built SNARC.)

shotList.setting: a field at dusk: the book's shadow lengthens into night; snow begins
shotList.purpose: The cold year: a Turing Award, and Congress narrowing military research to 'a direct and apparent relationship'. Snow density is a labelled qualitative ramp.

shotList.setting: a boarding-house window at night; a small lamp left on the sill
shotList.purpose: Pitts dies alone on 14 May 1969; McCulloch four months later. Restraint: the lamp, a hold, no dramatisation.

shotList.setting: a single candle; a book opening to a handwritten line
shotList.purpose: 11 July 1971: Rosenblatt drowns sailing on his 43rd birthday (no weather, no implication). The next printing: 'In memory of Frank Rosenblatt'. Hold in silence.

shotList.setting: a raised lecture platform in Britain; a televised debate across a candle
shotList.purpose: Lighthill and the 'combinatorial explosion'; the debate; UK funding falls for almost a decade. Fair line: true, narrow theorems read as a verdict, one cause among several; Papert's 'Snow White' card.

shotList.setting: the winter map: a snowbound paper landscape at night with a few lit windows
shotList.purpose: The lamplighters: Amari, a Helsinki thesis on rounding errors (the clue filed under the wrong subject), Werbos (disputed), Fukushima at a broadcaster's lab. 'Nobody in the warm houses was looking at these windows. That is what a winter is.'

shotList.setting: the low winter candle; at the very rim of its light, a desk; the Wall beside the board
shotList.purpose: Sussex, 1976: a tall young man, seated at a desk at the edge of the light (unnamed for now; never standing in this era). The chess slip yellows and curls. Clue card: scissors making two cuts, tied to the Helsinki thesis.

chapters.title: Clue Three: The Messenger Who Runs Backward
chapters.summary: The thaw: Hopfield's Versailles talk that nobody remembered; the tall man's wandering desks to Toronto (seated). October 1986: a lantern network learns XOR as the messenger runs backward and the hidden-layer card comes down; the misty hills plant the fog. Fair credit (several inventors; the 1961 false clue returns). Meanwhile the rival suspect Knowledge has its boom (MYCIN, Cyc's 1985 'practically nothing' put in the file), the 'AI Winter' is named in 1984 and Lisp machines go dark in 1987; Fodor and Pylyshyn stand at the rim of the connectionist light.
chapters.candle: INTELLIGENCE IS KNOWLEDGE, TYPED IN BY HAND (c. 7 rings, c. 1980–1987; a thin Cyc taper ~39)
chapters.turn: The messenger worked. And for the next fifteen years, almost nobody important wanted to hear from it.

shotList.setting: Versailles, summer 1981: the Hall of Mirrors, hundreds of mirrored silhouettes, none looking
shotList.purpose: A physicist presents a network; 'I have never met anyone who remembered hearing the talk.' Plant for the Nobel.

shotList.setting: parchment plate: an energy landscape of valleys
shotList.purpose: A ball rolls into a valley and a half-remembered pattern completes itself (memory as a valley).

shotList.setting: a sequence of desks at the rim of the light: San Diego, Cambridge, Pittsburgh, Toronto 1987
shotList.purpose: The tall man's wandering, seated at each desk; Toronto partly because US AI money was military. The Boltzmann machine as one flicker of cooling lanterns.

shotList.setting: 9 October 1986: a lantern network on a loom of strings
shotList.purpose: Real XOR training: light flows up, error glows, the messenger runs back and tugs each string by its share of the blame. The hidden-layer card comes down; hidden units find features (family trees).

shotList.setting: the misty hills at night: a traveller with a lantern
shotList.purpose: Gradient descent: he sees only the slope at his feet; a timid stride is trapped in a hollow, a bold one clears the ridge. Plant: the fog and its traps.

shotList.setting: the case board: the Helsinki thread lights; the 1961 caption card lifts
shotList.purpose: Who invented it? Several people, independently; the 1986 paper made it stick. The false clue returns. 'I have never claimed that I invented backpropagation.' NETtalk babbles then reads; a van steers through autumn woods.

shotList.setting: the stage: a second candle at the far end of the shelf; drawers of index cards like a sea
shotList.purpose: The rival suspect's candle lit: INTELLIGENCE IS KNOWLEDGE, TYPED IN BY HAND. MYCIN beats specialists in a blinded test, never used on a patient; Cyc begins.

shotList.setting: quote card filed into the manila folder
shotList.purpose: Cyc, 1985: 'practically nothing that current AI technology could draw from the raw text.' 'Put that in the file.' (refrain 4) Fifth Generation researchers at racks, not a menace.

shotList.setting: Austin 1984, then 1987: a room of cubicles whose screens go dark one by one
shotList.purpose: The 'AI Winter' named as a pun on nuclear winter; the Lisp-machine market collapses in about a year. The knowledge candle gutters at about seven rings; the thin Cyc taper keeps burning.

shotList.setting: the connectionist light; two figures at its rim
shotList.purpose: Fodor and Pylyshyn: 'John loves the girl…'; still argued in 2023. X-ray: hidden layers and a backward arrow glow. Clue card: a bead running backward on a string.

chapters.title: The Quiet Years
chapters.summary: Classical machine learning done justice. At Bell Labs a stencil learns ZIP codes from Buffalo mail ('Buffalo, twice') and later reads about one US check in ten: a winter of prestige, not of use. Vapnik's widest street and the SVM's one clean bowl (no fog, no traps) against the misty hills; Breiman's verdict. The candle NEURAL NETS ARE FIDDLY, AND BEATEN ANYWAY, with the holdouts' testimony at its rim. The 1995 dinner bet; the fading whisper and the LSTM's protected pipe; the chess slip comes down 29 years late. Ends on 'Why would anyone choose the fog?'
chapters.candle: NEURAL NETS ARE FIDDLY, AND BEATEN ANYWAY (c. 12 rings, frayed; late 1990s–c. 2009–12)
chapters.turn: One clean bowl. No fog. No traps. So why would anyone choose the fog?

shotList.setting: Holmdel, 1988–89: a gooseneck camera over a handwritten digit under a desk lamp
shotList.purpose: A pierced tin stencil slides over the digit (brief preview); ZIP codes from Buffalo mail. 'Buffalo, twice.'

shotList.setting: a bank's back room, 1996: a cheque sorter running
shotList.purpose: 'It is deployed commercially and reads several million cheques per day'; about one check in ten (LeCun's estimate). 'A winter of prestige, not of use.'

shotList.setting: Vapnik's blackboard becomes the widest empty street between two crowds of lanterns; then a single clean bowl
shotList.purpose: SVMs with support vectors on the kerb; the landscape is one clean bowl, no fog, no traps, set against the misty hills. Breiman's quote card. The fairest case for the age's belief.

shotList.setting: the stage: the 1990s candle; small hand-lanterns at its rim
shotList.purpose: Candle lit. At the rim: LeCun, the tall man at a Toronto window, Bengio in Montréal; testimony cards ('couldn't get our papers published', 'the worst possible time', 'This is crazy…'); the 'Deep Learning conspiracy'.

shotList.setting: Bell Labs, 14 March 1995: one typed sheet on a table, three signatures
shotList.purpose: The Jackel–Vapnik bet, LeCun as witness. Red-thread card: 'Who paid for dinner?'

shotList.setting: a long line of lanterns passing a whisper; a protected pipe
shotList.purpose: Vanishing gradients: the error fades like a whisper down a long line; the LSTM pipe carries it over a thousand steps. Plant for ch10.

shotList.setting: the Wall of Forecasts beside the board
shotList.purpose: May 1997: the chess slip comes down, 29 years late, won by search with no neural learning. The year 2000 passes and Turing's slip curls.

shotList.setting: the case board; the fog card pinned on red thread
shotList.purpose: Clue card: a pierced tin stencil and a pipe. Close on the new card: 'Why would anyone choose the fog?'

chapters.title: Two Accomplices: Data and Fire
chapters.summary: The dinner bet resolves (each man lost one). The 2006 belief that deep nets must be warmed up layer by layer is lit ('All three conditions are now satisfied' — they were nearly right). Accomplice one, data: Fei-Fei Li's nineteen-year estimate, tenure advice and nearly fifty thousand crowd workers in 167 countries. Accomplice two, fire: gaming cards, a seventy-fold speed-up, 'good old on-line back-propagation' with no warming up, the rectifier, and phones already hearing through neural nets. The pre-training candle gutters; the word will come back in a different coat.
chapters.candle: DEEP NETS MUST BE WARMED UP LAYER BY LAYER (c. 5 rings, frayed; 2006–c. 2010–12)
chapters.turn: Keep an eye on that word, pre-training. It will come back wearing a different coat.

shotList.setting: the red thread: the dinner card
shotList.purpose: 'Who paid for dinner?' Each man lost one. The card comes down.

shotList.setting: the stage: the 2006 candle; the tall man at its rim (standing allowed from the mid-2000s)
shotList.purpose: Candle lit; the paper's last line on a card: 'All three conditions are now satisfied.' — 'They were nearly right.'

shotList.setting: Princeton 2007, then a dark globe whose windows light up one by one
shotList.purpose: Accomplice one, data: about nineteen years by hand ('no graduate students would want to do this project!'), tenure advice, 'In summer 2008, we discovered crowdsourcing', almost fifty thousand workers in 167 countries. A mosaic of thumbnails folds into a tree.

shotList.setting: a gaming card held up to the lamp; its fans spin up like small furnaces
shotList.purpose: Accomplice two, fire: cards not built for this, seventy times faster; 'good old on-line back-propagation' with no warming up; the rectifier.

shotList.setting: summer 2012: a phone glowing in a hand on a dark street
shotList.purpose: Phones already hearing through neural networks, about three months before Florence.

shotList.setting: the shelf: the 2006 candle gutters with a frayed rim and a 'c.' tag
shotList.purpose: The pre-training candle goes out (end date interpretive). X-ray: racks of cards and a sea of text glow. Clue card: two small furnaces.

chapters.title: DEEP DIVE — The Night in Florence
chapters.summary: AlexNet in the five-beat grammar, with a teaching promise. The belief (features designed by experts; 28.2% and 25.8%), the bedroom with two gaming cards, then the machine built part by part: a photo as a grid of lights, one stencil and its worked number, stencils on stencils in a cathedral of true layer shapes, stencils learned from noise by the 1986 messenger, the weir and the ladle, ten bits per label against sixty million numbers (crops, mirrors, dropout), two towers that specialised without being told, five days downhill with the stride cut by hand three times. Florence, 12 October 2012: 15.3% against 26.2% (an ensemble of seven; best single net 18.2%). What lasted, fair credit to IDSIA, the 'waiting' prophecy, and the honest note that convolution is not part of the suspect.
chapters.candle: TO SEE, A MACHINE NEEDS FEATURES DESIGNED BY EXPERTS (13 rings, 1999–2012) goes out; LEARNED FEATURES, GIVEN DATA AND ARITHMETIC is lit (still burning)
chapters.turn: Put that in the file. And not every clue is a part of the suspect.

shotList.setting: a craftsman's workshop: tin stencils cut by hand, fed to a judge's lectern; a leaderboard of lanterns
shotList.purpose: Teaching promise. Beat 1, the belief and why it was reasonable: experts design features; 28.2% (2010), about 25.8% (2011). Candle lit.

shotList.setting: Toronto, 2011: a bedroom with a tower PC, two gaming cards, fans whining
shotList.purpose: A student who believed performance would scale with data talks a friend into trying; the friend writes the code. 'According to the Computer History Museum, a bedroom' (NVIDIA says a lab). Desk lamp → GPU LED match cut.

shotList.setting: match cut: the Mark I's 20×20 photocell eye becomes a 224×224×3 grid
shotList.purpose: A photo is just a grid of lights (numbers).

shotList.setting: a pierced 3×3 tin lantern sliding over a stitched '4'; its light on the wall
shotList.purpose: Beat 2–3: convolution as a stencil and a wall; the real rectified dot product fills the feature map; one cell worked on parchment.

shotList.setting: the cathedral of stencils rising block by block from a rose window that is the photograph
shotList.purpose: 96 stencils, then stencils on stencils: edges → textures → parts → things; true face widths 55, 27, 13, 13, 13; three great halls; a thousand doors; about sixty million numbers. 'So the depth really is important…'

shotList.setting: the cathedral stairs; noise tiles resolving into a mosaic
shotList.purpose: Nobody cut them: the stencils begin as noise and are learned as the messenger from ch05 runs down the stairs.

shotList.setting: a weir and a ladle on parchment
shotList.purpose: The rectifier (a weir; about six times faster to train) and overlapping pooling (a ladle that keeps the brightest bead).

shotList.setting: a scale tipping; a hall of shifted mirrors; half the lanterns snuffed
shotList.purpose: About ten bits per label against sixty million numbers: crops and mirrors make more pictures; dropout snuffs half the lanterns on every example (p = 0.5).

shotList.setting: the cathedral's two towers joined by a few bridges of light
shotList.purpose: Two cards that talk only at certain layers; unbidden, one tower learns colourless edges and the other colour blobs, every run. Plant: nobody told them. On screen only: ≈96% of numbers vs ≈92% of arithmetic.

shotList.setting: the misty hills at night; the bedroom window frosting
shotList.purpose: Five days downhill: many small steps, the stride cut by hand three times, about ninety passes.

shotList.setting: Florence, Friday 12 October 2012, 17:05: a crowded hall kept generic
shotList.purpose: Beat 4, the night it was tested: the last talk of the session; the professor could not sit, so could not fly (an empty place); by Li's account LeCun stood at the back.

shotList.setting: the result plate: a row of lanterns at one height, one dropping far lower
shotList.purpose: Fifteen point three against twenty-six point two; caption: seven networks together; best single network 18.2% on validation.

shotList.setting: the workshop's stencils hanging unused; the shelf; a new candle lit
shotList.purpose: Beat 5, what lasted: every top-five team used convnets within a year; fair credit (IDSIA's earlier wins, road signs 2011); the CHM before/after card; Hinton's quip card. The expert-features candle goes out at thirteen rings; LEARNED FEATURES, GIVEN DATA AND ARITHMETIC is lit. The fog card comes down.

shotList.setting: the Wall of Forecasts; a GPU LED multiplying into a distant aisle; the X-ray box
shotList.purpose: The prophecy slip: '…simply by waiting for faster GPUs and bigger datasets…' — 'Put that in the file.' (refrain 5). 'Not every clue is a part of the suspect': convolution does not light in the box. Clue card: a tile from the 96 filters.

chapters.title: The Gold Rush
chapters.summary: Four held images and a quiet plant. Lake Tahoe, December 2012: a man who had not sat for seven years stands at a laptop on an upturned wastebasket and auctions a three-person company (per Cade Metz), at the centre of the new light. Words become places (king − man + woman near queen). Go: Coulom's 'maybe ten years' slip glints early as move 37 and Lee Sedol's move 78 play out; the candle lasts about two rings. A panda becomes a 'gibbon'; a lab is founded with hope and fear in one sentence. Hinton's 'graduate student' slip is pinned without comment.
chapters.candle: A GO MACHINE IS A DECADE AWAY (2 rings, 2014–2016)

shotList.setting: Harrah's, Lake Tahoe, December 2012: Room 731, a laptop on an upturned wastebasket
shotList.purpose: Hinton, standing, in the centre of the new candle's light, auctions a three-person company by email and stops at forty-four million dollars (per Cade Metz).

shotList.setting: a star-field of words with an arrow copied from 'man' to 'woman'
shotList.purpose: Words become places: king − man + woman lands near queen, once king itself is ruled out.

shotList.setting: Seoul, March 2016: a Go board under a hanging lamp; the Wall's 2014 slip
shotList.purpose: Coulom's 'maybe ten years'; move 37 (one in ten thousand), then Lee Sedol's move 78, also rated one in ten thousand, which won humanity's only game. The pin glints; the candle burns about two rings.

shotList.setting: a panda, a veil of faint noise, a 'gibbon'
shotList.purpose: Doubt from inside the rush: imperceptible noise turns a panda into a 99.3% gibbon. December 2015: a lab founded with benefit and damage in one sentence.

shotList.setting: the far end of the Wall of Forecasts, in silence
shotList.purpose: September 2017: a slip goes up, 'The future depends on some graduate student who is deeply suspicious of everything I have said.' No comment.

chapters.title: DEEP DIVE — Everything Looks at Everything
chapters.summary: The Transformer in the five-beat grammar, with a teaching promise. The belief that language must be read in order (a slow scribe, the whisper from ch06), the 2014 bottleneck and its highlighter, and the people (a lunch, doubters at the rim, a twenty-year-old intern from Hinton's Toronto lab, an engineer who overheard and rewrote the code). The machine part by part: fire the reader and keep the highlighter; three cards; the worked number for 'bank'; why divide by eight; 'it' → 'animal' with eight heads; positions as clock hands; talk then think, six times. The night it was tested (five minutes before the deadline, random author order), why it won (one big multiplication, twelve hours on one machine, a seventh of the compute) and its n² catch. What lasted, the honest sentence, and the curtain over the future that turns a translator into a writer.
chapters.candle: LANGUAGE MUST BE READ IN ORDER (20 rings, 1997–2017)
chapters.turn: Hide the future, and ask the machine, over and over: what comes next?

shotList.setting: a long hall of hanging word-slips; a scribe passing a single lamp down the line
shotList.purpose: Teaching promise. Beat 1: the belief, reasonable for twenty years; the whisper fades down the line; 'If you have a thousand words, you have to wait for a thousand cycles.' Candle lit.

shotList.setting: parchment heat-map between English and French word-slips
shotList.purpose: Squeezing a sentence into one vector was 'a bottleneck'; attention lets the translator look back at every word (the map bends where French reorders).

shotList.setting: Mountain View, 2016–17: couches, whiteboards, a cafe table; the case board's red thread from Toronto
shotList.purpose: A suggestion over lunch; doubt at the rim (a colleague's 'biggest incorrect prediction of my life', a father at the dinner table); a twenty-year-old intern from Hinton's Toronto lab (red thread on the board); an engineer overhears and rewrites the code, after which it finally got better.

shotList.setting: the hall: the scribe vanishes and every slip lights at once
shotList.purpose: Fire the reader, keep the highlighter: '…dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely.'

shotList.setting: each word-slip grows a small lantern, a mirror and a sealed note
shotList.purpose: Three cards: a question (query), a label (key), a message (value).

shotList.setting: parchment arithmetic for 'crossed the river bank'; a jug pouring into four lantern-glass cups
shotList.purpose: Beat 3, the worked number (labelled illustrative): scores 2, 0, 4, 2; halved; softmax 0.20 / 0.07 / 0.53 / 0.20; 'bank' turns water-blue.

shotList.setting: the same jug shown twice: frozen and soft
shotList.purpose: Why divide by eight: unscaled, the jug tips everything into one cup and learning freezes; ÷√64 keeps it soft.

shotList.setting: the hall of slips: 'The animal didn't cross the street because it was too tired'
shotList.purpose: 'it' looks back at 'animal'; thread width = computed weight; eight heads in eight low-chroma hues ask different questions at once.

shotList.setting: wave barcodes on each slip; a clock face with three hands
shotList.purpose: Where am I? Each position wears a barcode of waves, like a clock's second, minute and hour hands.

shotList.setting: a loom of light: ribbons through looms and lanterns, six storeys
shotList.purpose: Talk, then think, six times; a highway lane carries the original past every step (toy weights labelled).

chapters.title: Read Everything
chapters.summary: Pre-training returns in a new coat. Cyc's 1985 card is set beside GPT-2's one-line objective ('In 1985, that was a perfectly sensible thing to believe'), and the typesetter's case answers the prologue's 'no rulebook'. GPT-2 withheld and released in stages ('too dangerous' was a headline). The straight line on log paper, GPT-3's hundred and seventy-five billion, the 'waiting' slip glinting, the Bitter Lesson; readers spot GPT-3's articles only about 52% of the time (an echo of Turing, not a pass). Chinchilla corrects the recipe; the doubters crowd the rim (octopus, parrots, Gebru's exit in two voices, Marcus).
chapters.candle: SCALE IS THE MAIN LEVER (2020–, still burning) · GROW THE MODEL FASTER THAN THE DATA (2 rings, 2020–2022)
chapters.turn: It had read nearly everything. It still didn't know what we wanted.

chapters.title: The Last Accomplice, and the Return to the Scene
chapters.summary: The gardener: a simulated robot learns a backflip from nine hundred human choices (Turing's child machine, educated), and InstructGPT's small model is preferred to a hundred-times-larger one. Anthropic's founding told plainly (no founder count; its self-description; FTX money; Constitutional AI with its caveat). A 2022 belief that a chatbot is sentient echoes 1958, undecided. Then the return to the dark room, 30 November 2022: not a new engine but a new door. The X-ray is complete; the launch post's admission and Rosenblatt's 1961 sentence about language are read over the box. A one-breath stampede. 'Case solved?' 'Not quite.'

chapters.title: The Case Reopened
chapters.summary: May 2023: a pan along the Wall of Forecasts finds a slip that has been there all along, and the tall man, standing, takes down his own '30 to 50 years' forecast; in fairness, 'Google has acted very responsibly'; he walks from the centre of the light back to its rim ('Persistence is not the same as certainty'). A new candle of worry is lit with the one-sentence extinction statement. The debate splits into three lamps (existential worry, present harms, doom-scepticism), two Turing laureates in the light and one at its edge. Five days in November at OpenAI, reasons attributed and still disputed.
chapters.candle: SMARTER-THAN-HUMAN AI MAY BE YEARS AWAY, AND DANGEROUS (2023–, still burning)
chapters.turn: The case had reopened. And it was no longer confined to one country.

chapters.title: Two Shores
chapters.summary: The US–China race as dated beliefs on two equally warm shores with a shared Go board on a jetty. 2017's plan names no rival; October 2022's fence of rule pages and Beijing's reply in its own words light COMPUTE IS THE CHOKEPOINT. A small price tag on a vast building (one run's rented-chip price, by DeepSeek's own accounting); R1 released and its founder at the Premier's symposium the same day; a week later the largest one-day market loss in US history: a struck match, out within a day, with fair dissent ('7-10 months'; 'not adversaries'). Open weights cross the water; talent; allegations as allegations. Rivals still sign the same pages (Bletchley, Lima, a September 2026 channel with two names). THE GAP IS MONTHS still burns.
chapters.candle: COMPUTE IS THE CHOKEPOINT (c. 2 rings, 2022–2025) · the struck match (27 Jan 2025, one day) · THE GAP IS MONTHS (2025–, still burning)
chapters.turn: As of October 2026, nobody knows who is ahead. Everyone agrees it's close.

Candle lit, still burning: THE GAP IS MONTHS (estimates from a chip-seller's 'nanoseconds behind America in AI', Nov 2025, said with a commercial stake, to months, to a compute deficit; do not use the Sept 2025 'nanoseconds' line as being about AI).

chapters.title: Case Status: Open
chapters.summary: The fast-forward and the reveal. A phone at 2 a.m. in a cheap hotel: a Nobel shared with the physicist whose Versailles talk nobody remembered, now ninety-one. What the suspect does now: thinking behind a curtain; a model that picks 'rabbit' before writing the line ('Nobody told it to plan'); METR's ruler running out at sixteen hours beside a trial in which developers were slower. Every lab under the same light, as of October 2026. The last witnesses at the rim and the closing irony. Widrow's death at ninety-five and Mechanical Turk's closure five days ago: the oldest witnesses leave the room. The rewind plays forward, the board becomes a lantern network with one lantern dark, the shelf becomes a bar chart in wax, the last slip is read, STATUS: OPEN, and a hand from the viewer's side lights a new unlettered candle on an unresolved chord. Turing's closing line; disclosure card.
chapters.candle: the shelf seen whole (a bar chart in wax); a new unlettered candle lit by the viewer's hand
chapters.turn: The case is not closed. It never is. Somewhere tonight a lamp is on, and someone is suspicious. Perhaps it's you.
